To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a rank-based approach for hierarchical data classification is more robust and scalable than existing methods, and that the proposed approach is able to learn a more accurate hierarchical classification model than existing methods.

we developed a hierarchical classification approach using rank based loss functions that outperform other baselines on several datasets and we also developed a scalable distributed implementation of our approach.
rank-based hierarchical classifiers can be used to classify instances into hierarchies with improved performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a hierarchical classification framework that utilizes the rank-based loss functions for training the per-node classifiers.
the problem of developing scalable hierarchical classification approaches that can effectively utilize the inherent structure of the underlying databases.
the development and evaluation of a novel hierarchical classification framework that is scalable and robust to noisy data and large number of nodes within the hierarchy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rank-based hierarchical classification approach is able to provide improved performance in comparison to the baseline methods on several datasets.
our proposed approach is a novel and effective hierarchical classification method.

we present an efficient distributed approach for training a hierarchical classification model that uses a rank-based loss to differentiate between the training examples from different nodes within the hierarchy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed rank-based approach can be used as a general framework for training hierarchical classification models.
the proposed approach is able to improve the classification accuracy by 5-15% over the baseline approaches on the hierarchical classification task.

we have developed a scalable hierarchical classification approach that can be trained on very large scale databases and also achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark hierarchical datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a hierarchical ranking-based approach for classifying data within hierarchical databases can be a useful tool in several applications such as image classification and protein function classification.
a simple rank-based approach can be used for hierarchical classification, and can lead to significant performance improvements.
by incorporating a rank-based loss during training we can improve the performance of a hierarchical classifier.
